recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-21297 unless OO later reopens the broader Vital Signs profile policy and decides to support non-point-in-time or calculated vital-sign-related observations within these profiles.
issue_request: FHIR-21297 was an Applied OO R6 change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking to profile Period out of the Blood Pressure profile because blood pressure is captured at a single point in time. The final resolution expanded the change to the Vital Signs effective[x] choices because all Vital Signs profile LOINC codes are point-in-time values.
initial_application: Commit af25d09edb removed Period from source/observation/structuredefinition-profile-vitalsigns.xml and changed the effective[x] wording to state that vital signs are point-in-time measurements recorded using dateTime. Commit 59db19eb59 removed remaining profile-summary references to effectivePeriod.
additional_context: Observation is active in source/fhir.ini, and Blood Pressure derives from the Vital Signs Base profile. The linked OO Zulip thread and Confluence minutes show the work group considered applying the restriction at the base profile, including average blood pressure concerns. Later related issues FHIR-50075, FHIR-50194, and FHIR-41426 clarified category/profile applicability for calculated and de-identified observations without reversing the FHIR-21297 dateTime-only decision; FHIR-50194 is already represented by a separate combined-branch audit commit.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because no source edit is needed. Current source already removes Period from the active Vital Signs effective[x] definition, Blood Pressure inherits that restriction, the summary no longer mentions effectivePeriod, and the current narrative clarifies point-in-time scope for calculated vital-sign-related observations.
